text:
Application promotion readiness

The platform typically evaluates predefined promotion gates. A release advances only when required checks pass, evidence is recorded, blocking defects are resolved or accepted, and the responsible people approve it.

Development to testing

- Code is committed, reviewed, and traceable to requirements or work items.
- The application builds successfully and deploys consistently.
- Unit tests, static analysis, dependency checks, and basic security scans pass.
- Required configuration, test data, and deployment artifacts are available.
- No unresolved defect blocks meaningful testing.

Testing to production

- Functional, integration, regression, and acceptance criteria are satisfied.
- Required performance, security, accessibility, compatibility, and reliability checks pass.
- Critical defects are closed; remaining risks are documented and explicitly accepted.
- Production configuration, data migration, monitoring, support, backup, recovery, and rollback procedures are ready.
- Testers provide validation evidence, the product owner accepts the outcome, and authorized technical or business owners approve release.

These gates are often enforced in a delivery pipeline using pass or fail rules, quality thresholds, signed approvals, audit records, and deployment policies. After deployment, health checks and monitoring confirm the release; failed checks can pause rollout or trigger rollback.
